disclosure: FILED AFTER THE IMPLEMENTATION, NOT BEFORE IT. The dispatch asks for the delta to be measured 'first, at a named ref, and state it before writing code', and this file does not do that: the code was written, merged (PR #68, 7dda6db0) and deployed before this checkpoint existed. That is a deviation from the dispatch and it is recorded rather than papered over. What the file can still be is honest about its own timing: every figure below was re-measured AFTER the merge, by reading the pre-lane revision `fd8562c` out of git and running the lane's own instrument against it, so nothing here rests on the lane's memory of what it did. Where the retrospective reading differs from the lane's own account of its work, the difference is reported below under `theLaneWasWorseThanItThought`.

theInstrumentFinding.whyTheyAreIdentical: template-city is the FIXTURE pack. src/server.mjs only takes the real-source branch when `pack.generatesFixtures !== true`, so on template-city the live MyGov mappers this lane corrected are never executed and the demo generators' own already-opaque rows are drawn. Identical input, identical output, identical verdict.
theInstrumentFinding.whyThisIsThePointAndNotAnObjection: This is the dispatch's own premise measured rather than quoted: 'A pass on `template-city` is not a pass.' The instrument is not broken and it is not vacuous - it reads 400 table cells and 71 refused-column cells off both surfaces, and the mutation harness catches 4 of 4 planted defects on BOTH artifacts (see `bothDirectionsOnTheBuiltSurface`). What it cannot do is compare two revisions that differ only in a code path the fixture pack never enters. A close that cited the template-city pass as evidence for the four corrections would be citing an instrument that provably cannot fire on them.
theInstrumentFinding.whatWouldMakeItFire: A built surface whose table cells and load-strip cells were composed from LIVE Bastrop records. Which is bastrop_tx, and which is why the dispatch puts the proof there.

bothDirectionsOnTheBuiltSurface.note: Recorded here because it is the half of the argument that does NOT depend on the live pack, and because it is the strongest evidence available that the instrument itself works.

whatEachMutantProved: 1: a named person in the load strip -> the check refuses person-shaped text on a published workload ranking
2: a Place tab spliced into the strip -> 'tab strip is [Place, Pipeline, Inspections, Work orders, Code enforcement, Licenses, Plan review, Flood study]'
3: licence rows re-ordered out of the design's band-then-expiry order -> 'licence rows are out of the design's order [expires in 269 days, ... expired 29 days ago]'

bothDirectionsOnTheBuiltSurface.whatThisDoesNotProve: That the PRE-LANE PRODUCT was defective. A mutation harness proves the check can fire, not that a given revision violates it. On the fixture pack the pre-lane revision violates nothing.

theLaneWasWorseThanItThought.workOrderFreeText: The dispatch asked to 'confirm no work-order free text reaches a rendered field'. The pre-lane revision did not pass that check: `row.title` backed the Subject cell. The lane had treated the work-order position as a confirmation exercise; measured at the named ref it was a live defect on a rendered cell beside an address, and it is the one the four-corrections list does not name explicitly.
theLaneWasWorseThanItThought.theOfficerFilterIsAWiderLeakThanTheColum: The dispatch names 'a per-officer count on a published screen'. At fd8562c the leak is wider than the column: `distinctValues(records, "officerRef")` populates the officer FILTER from the same field, so the names were also the filter's option labels - an enumeration of the department's officers, not only a name per row.
theLaneWasWorseThanItThought.theInstrumentCouldNotHaveToldUs: Every one of these is invisible on template-city, so a lane that proved itself on the default pack would have shipped all four while its instrument stayed green. That is the measured argument for the bastrop_tx proof, and it is the reason `theInstrumentFinding` is the first section above the board-by-board.

preRegisteredFalsifiers: F1 - The four corrections must be DERIVED from the live record, not from a list of known names. Violation: feed a record whose applicant/inspector/officer/businessName is a name this repo has never seen and confirm the refusal fires and the reference is stable across rows that share it. A whitelist of the captured names passes every read and fails this.

F2 - The refusal must be a REFUSAL, not a classifier. Violation: feed 'Hill Country Homes' (a business) and 'Deborah Ann Moore' (a person) through the same dimension and confirm the surface does not keep one and drop the other by shape. Both directions must be REFUSED or the rule is a guess wearing a rule's clothes.

F3 - The licence order must be the design's comparator, not the source's order. Violation: return the same rows in a different source order and confirm the rendered order does not move. A surface that renders source order passes on a friendly feed and fails this.
F4 - A free-text field must back NO rendered cell. Violation: plant a citizen name and phone number into row.title and confirm it reaches no cell on the work-orders board.

F5 - The instrument must be observed FAILING as well as passing. Violation: the four mutants in scripts/prove-dev-services-corrections.mjs, plus the unmutated control, which is what keeps 'caught 4' from meaning 'fails everything'.

F6 - The delta must be measured on the LIVE pack. Violation: run the instrument on template-city and observe that it passes on both revisions - which is exactly what happened, and is the finding this checkpoint leads with. A lane whose delta is invisible to its own instrument on the pack it defaulted to has not measured anything.

subAgents.note: FAN-DEPTH 0. This lane launched no sub-agents.

leave_behind: THE INSTRUMENT DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE ON THE FIXTURE PACK, AND THE CHECK'S OWN OUTPUT WILL NOT SAY SO. `check.mjs --dir` returns exit 0 with 400 matched table cells on a surface that leaks four classes of personal data, because the live mappers never run on a `generatesFixtures: true` pack. Any future reader who points this check at a template-city export and sees '1 built file(s) pass' should read it as 'the demo pack is not the place this rule can fire', never as 'this lens publishes no personal data'.

THE PRE-LANE REVISION IS EXTRACTED AND STILL ON DISK. P:\smartcity-dashboards-worktrees\g154-prelane is a detached worktree at fd8562c with node_modules junctioned to the lane worktree's. It is the control for every figure in this checkpoint and it costs nothing to keep until the close is read; the junction will break if the lane worktree is removed, which is harmless (it can be re-made).

`scripts/export-dev-services-lens.mjs` REPORTS A PER-TAB SETTLE COUNT THAT IS NOISY AND SHOULD NOT BE QUOTED. One in-process run printed '0, 86, 86, 14, 86, 86, 86' rows across the seven tabs because the probe samples the DOM while the app is still re-rendering; the written artifact was complete in every case (64,619 bytes, and the check read 57 rows and 400 cells out of it). The authoritative matched-input count is check.mjs's own line, not this probe. Not fixed in this lane.
